title: Conservative and Nonconservative Forces
theory:
**Big idea:** For some forces, a round trip costs nothing. For others, like friction, every trip costs energy.

**Two equivalent definitions of a conservative force**
1. The work done in **any round trip is zero**, or
2. The work done depends **only on the initial and final positions**, not on the path.

| Conservative | Nonconservative |
|---|---|
| Gravity | Friction |
| Coulomb (electric) force | Air drag and other resistances |
| Spring force | |

**Friction on a round trip**
A block (mass m, friction coefficient μ) is dragged a distance l to the right and then back to its start.
- Going right, friction points left: W = –μmgl.
- Coming back, friction points right: W = –μmgl again.
- **Round trip: W = –2μmgl**, not zero!

**🧮 Example:** m = 2 kg, μ = 0.2, l = 5 m, g = 10 m/s². W = –2 × 0.2 × 2 × 10 × 5 = **–40 J**.

**A spring-block on a rough table:** each time the block passes the centre, it moves a little more slowly. The configuration is the same, but the kinetic energy is really lost. Friction is the culprit, and eventually the block stops.

> ⚠️ **Common mistake:** Thinking friction does zero work on a round trip, the way gravity does. Friction always opposes the motion, so it does negative work on both legs.

questions.prompt: A force is called conservative if the work done by it:

options.text: In any round trip is zero

questions.explanation: Zero work in every round trip, or equivalently, path-independent work.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a **nonconservative** force?
questions.explanation: Friction does negative work on both legs of a round trip.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg block is dragged 5 m to the right and then back to its starting point on a rough floor (μ = 0.2, g = 10 m/s²). The total work done by friction is:
The work done by a conservative force between two points:

options.text: Depends only on the initial and final positions
Depends on the speed of the body

questions.explanation: Path independence is the second definition of a conservative force.

questions.prompt: A block attached to a spring oscillates on a rough table. Each time it passes the centre, its speed is smaller than before because:

options.text: Friction, a nonconservative force, removes mechanical energy

questions.explanation: Friction turns mechanical energy into heat, so it is not stored and returned.
